title: Tessera credentials onramp — sticky notes
content:
Meeting notes (quick capture) - 2025-02-11 call with Tessera Credentials

Attendees:
- Laura Benton (Tessera CTO)
- Evan Park (Tessera Eng Lead)
- Samir Cho (Tessera Security)
- Ravi Suresh (Redwood SE)
- Maya Alvarez (Redwood Solutions)

High-level ask:
- Replace brittle rule-based PII scrubbing in their KYC intake with a conversational assistant that extracts structured identity fields (name, dob, id_type, id_number masked) and returns verification confidence.
- Must run inside customer VPC (private deployment) OR via Dedicated with strict KMS/HSM key controls.
- Zero permanent storage of raw ID images or raw extracted PII on Redwood side. Tokens-only telemetry ok if pseudonymized.

Constraints / non-negotiables from Tessera:
- Data residency: EU-only for EU customers.
- Keys: customer-managed KMS; hardware-backed keys for signing verification artifacts.
- Throughput: peak 35 reqs/min, typical 8–12 reqs/min. Burst tolerance up to 80/min for short windows.
- Latency SLO: 500ms p95 for text-only verification, 1.2s p95 for flows that include OCR + image embedding.
- Audit logs accessible via S3 (encrypted) within their AWS account.

Technical notes / gotchas we should call out:
- OCR + LLM split: prefer OCR in-customer (edge) then send extracted text + embedding to Redwood. Sending images increases private-deploy footprint and complicates KMS flow.
- Tokenization surprise: scanned ID lines (long numeric strings) tokenizes oddly -> causes hallucinated id split. Need explicit prompt templates to ask for contiguous numeric capture and validation regex.
- Streaming: if we stream parsing progress back to UI, make sure partial KV cache is not flushed to logs. Streaming gate for PII redaction must be explicit.
- Embeddings for image features: customer wants image embedding similarity for tamper detection. We should recommend using 1536-d embeddings (float16 quantized) and store hashes in their S3. Make explicit: embeddings are still subject to compliance.
- Rate-limiter interplay: Tessera has global gateway in front of Redwood. Need backpressure signals from Redwood if Dedicated bursts exceed reserved slots. Plan for graceful 429 handling and client-side retry jitter.
- Warmup: small steady warmup is required to keep cold-start sensitive models under SLO. Recommend a 10-min warm window with 5-10 synthetic prefix prompts every 2 minutes during peak hours.

Suggested onramp plan (v0 -> v1):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): quick PoC in Dedicated with redaction-only pipeline. Deliverables: sample flow, latency numbers, basic audit log stub. JIRA:TESS-234.
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): VPC private deployment option, KMS integration, OCR handshake. Deliverables: infra runbook, canary rollout plan, A/B test harness. JIRA:TESS-241, JIRA:TESS-256.
- Phase 2 (Q2): production rollout + batch reconciliation, quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to golden prompt sets.

Action items (owner, due) — immediate:
- Ravi: write up minimal architecture diagram (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and share with Laura by 2025-02-14. (TODO: include edge OCR pros/cons slide)
- Maya: infra sizing + cost sketch for Dedicated pool to sustain 80/min bursts and 500ms p95 target by 2025-02-18.
- Noah: quick prompt templates (3 variants) for numeric ID capture + validation regex examples by 2025-02-16.
- Tessera (Evan): scoped list of 5 sample ID image types and representative OCR outputs (anonymized) by 2025-02-20.

Implementation details to surface in follow-up:
- Prompt template (example):
  "You are a strict extractor. Given OCR text, output JSON with keys name, dob, id_type, id_number_masked (mask all but last 4 digits) and confidence. Validate id_number against this regex: ^\\d{8,12}$; if not valid, return error_code: INVALID_FORMAT."

- SDK notes: recommend short-lived per-request tokens minted by Tessera via a Redwood STS-style exchange. Avoid long-lived API keys attached to user sessions.

Testing and quality metrics:
- Unit tests for prompt failures (simulate OCR garbage) -> expected fail mode should be consistent error payload.
- End-to-end regression suite: 50 golden examples (split EU/US) stitched into Redwood Optimize monitors.
- Data drift alerts when distribution of token lengths for id_number changes > 2 std devs.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do they need signed attestation artifacts (verifiable by third parties)? If yes, HSM signing flow requirements need more scoping (Ravi to confirm).
- How strict is OCR must-run-inside-customer? They mentioned preferring it but not absolute. Confirm during tech sync.
- Disaster recovery: wanted 24-hour RPO for logs. Are they ok to own S3 lifecycle or want Redwood-managed snapshots?

Random notes to self:
- Watch out for token leakage in earlier PoC: scrub any sample outputs before uploading to Confluence.
- Check past private-deploy KMS runbook (confluence link above) for example IAM roles mapping.
- Consider adding a small prompt-level deterministic checksum to outputs so Tessera can verify no midstream tampering happened.

Next meeting: schedule tech sync w/ Tessera eng + security (30–45m) — propose 2025-02-19 10:00 UTC. Include SRE and Eng Infra.

Quick checklist before next call:
- [ ] Arch diagram draft (Ravi)
- [ ] Dedicated sizing estimate (Maya)
- [ ] 3 prompt templates + validation rules (Noah)
- [ ] Customer anonymized OCR samples (Evan/Tessera)
- [ ] Initial JIRA epics created and linked to customer space

End of capture.
